title: Substitution versus frameshift: predict the protein

stimulus.title: A short coding sequence and three mutations
stimulus.html:
The table shows the first part of a normal mRNA and three mutant versions, each with one change. A codon table, grouped by amino acid, follows.

Normal and mutant mRNAs (5′ to 3′; positions counted from the A of the start codon)
mRNASequenceChange
NormalAUG UUC GGA CAU UGG AAA CCG UAG GC—
Mutation 1AUGUUUGGACAUUGGAAACCGUAGGCC at position 6 replaced by U
Mutation 2AUGUAUCGGACAUUGGAAACCGUAGGCA inserted after position 4
Mutation 3AUGUUCAGACAUUGGAAACCGUAGGCG at position 7 replaced by A

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe the effect of mutation 1 on the polypeptide, and explain why it has that effect.

rubric.point: Describes no change in the polypeptide (Met-Phe-Gly-His-Trp-Lys-Pro) and explains that the changed codon UUU still codes for phenylalanine, as UUC did (a silent mutation; the code is redundant).
accept: no change, because UUC and UUU both code for Phe
silent: the second codon becomes UUU, still phenylalanine
same protein since more than one codon codes for phenylalanine

parts.sample: Mutation 1 has no effect on the polypeptide: it is still Met-Phe-Gly-His-Trp-Lys-Pro. The change turns the second codon from UUC into UUU, and both codons code for phenylalanine, because the genetic code has more than one codon for most amino acids. This is a silent mutation.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Predict the first five amino acids of the polypeptide made from mutation 2.

rubric.point: Predicts Met-Tyr-Arg-Thr-Leu (reading AUG UAU CGG ACA UUG).

parts.sample: Regrouping the mutant mRNA in threes from the start codon gives AUG UAU CGG ACA UUG, so the first five amino acids are Met-Tyr-Arg-Thr-Leu.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why mutation 2 is more likely than mutation 3 to destroy the protein's function.

rubric.point: Explains that mutation 3 changes one codon/one amino acid (Gly to Arg) and leaves the rest normal, while mutation 2 adds one base and shifts the reading frame, changing every amino acid after it (and removing the normal stop codon from the frame or creating new stops).
accept: mutation 3 changes one amino acid but mutation 2 shifts the frame so all later amino acids change
frameshift alters every codon after the insertion; the substitution alters only one
mutation 2 is a frameshift; mutation 3 is missense, one amino acid replaced

parts.sample: Mutation 3 replaces one base, so only one codon changes (GGA, glycine, becomes AGA, arginine) and every other amino acid is normal. Mutation 2 inserts one base, which shifts the reading frame: every codon after the insertion is regrouped, so every amino acid after methionine changes and the normal stop codon is no longer read. A protein with almost its whole sequence changed is very unlikely to fold and work.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A different mutation inserts one A after position 18 instead of after position 4. Predict whether its effect on the protein would be larger or smaller than that of mutation 2, and justify your prediction.

rubric.point: Predicts a smaller effect and justifies it: the frame shifts only after codon 6, so the first six amino acids (Met-Phe-Gly-His-Trp-Lys) are normal and only the amino acids after the insertion change (Pro becomes Thr-Val-Gly…).
accept: smaller, because only the codons after position 18 are shifted; the first six amino acids are unchanged
smaller effect: a frameshift near the end changes fewer amino acids
less severe since Met-Phe-Gly-His-Trp-Lys stay the same

parts.sample: Smaller. An insertion after position 18 shifts the reading frame only from the seventh codon on, so the first six amino acids, Met-Phe-Gly-His-Trp-Lys, are the same as normal; only the amino acids after the insertion change (Thr-Val-Gly… instead of Pro and stop). Mutation 2 changes nearly every amino acid, so a late frameshift leaves much more of the protein intact.
